Job Description: As the Head of AI Platform Engineering – Execution Plane, you will lead the development and implementation of our enterprise platform’s execution layer including management of agentic AI workloads, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. You will: You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and technology partners to develop and integrate automation solutions that drive business growth, improve customer experiences, and reduce operational costs. You have: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, engineering, management or a related field. Strong people leadership experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and developing senior technical talent. Deep hands-on technical background designing, building, and operating production-grade distributed systems, AI/ML platforms, data platforms, or cloud-native runtime services. Experience leading teams responsible for the execution layer of a platform, including runtime services, model inference, retrieval, orchestration, tool invocation, workflow execution, or production AI operations. Ability to own the roadmap and delivery for execution plane capabilities such as model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, runtime adapters, MCP services, knowledge bases, retrieval pipelines, inference services, and deployment patterns. Strong understanding of data access patterns, enterprise APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector/search systems, context engineering, and governed access to systems of record. Experience building reliable, scalable, low-latency execution services with clear contracts, strong observability, graceful degradation, retry patterns, rate limits, and operational resilience. Ability to partner with control plane, developer experience, data engineering, security, architecture, operations, and domain application teams to ensure execution technologies operate behind governed platform interfaces. Proven ability to drive engineering excellence through design reviews, architecture standards, testing, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, incident response, SLOs, runbooks, and production support mechanisms. Strong understanding of enterprise security and compliance requirements for runtime execution, including identity propagation, auditability, data handling, least privilege access, secrets management, and environment isolation. Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to simplify complex runtime, data, and AI execution topics for senior stakeholders while aligning teams around reusable platform patterns. You will: Experience with agentic AI systems, LLM platforms, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. Experience with AWS-based AI execution services and cloud-native patterns, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, EKS, DynamoDB, S3, IAM, CloudWatch, and related DevOps tooling. Familiarity with RAG systems, enterprise search, vector databases, embedding models, rerankers, knowledge bases, context engineering, and governed retrieval from enterprise data sources. Experience designing multi-tenant runtime platforms with environment isolation, workload identities, RBAC/ABAC, cross-account access patterns, quotas, throttling, and secure service-to-service communication. Background in MLOps, LLMOps, AIOps, model lifecycle management, evaluation pipelines, model serving, inference optimization, or production AI operations. Experience with observability for AI workloads, including distributed tracing, token usage, latency, model/tool errors, cost attribution, quality metrics, safety metrics, and operational dashboards. Experience with performance, scalability, and cost optimization for high-volume runtime services, including caching, batching, streaming, load testing, capacity planning, and GPU/CPU optimization where applicable. Experience building reusable platform abstractions, SDKs, runtime adapters, reference architectures, or deployment templates that make execution technologies portable across vendors and use cases. Experience integrating enterprise tools, APIs, data services, and workflow systems through governed connectors rather than point-to-point application wiring. Comfort operating in a regulated, matrixed environment where production safety, auditability, resiliency, and vendor optionality are core design principles. At Guardian, we do the right thing, we believe people count, we courageously shape our future together, and we go above and beyond for the people we serve. Job Description: Position Summary Are you passionate about building strong client relationships and helping businesses maximize the value of their employee benefits programs? Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate renewals, plan alternatives, pricing strategies, and recommendations. Strong customer service, consultative, negotiation, persuasion, and influencing skills. Strong mathematical aptitude and analytical skills, including the ability to evaluate experience, utilization, pricing, and plan design options. Working knowledge of group insurance products, contracts, services, financing methodologies, and underwriting principles. Experience using Salesforce, GCRS, Siebel, CPS, Phoenix, Business Objects, or similar CRM and reporting platforms. Job Description: Position Summary The Head of Distribution Strategy partners with the Head of Distribution to convert the enterprise distribution strategy into an actionable growth plan. While the Head of Distribution sets the strategic direction, this role determines how and where the organization will compete, evaluates expansion opportunities, develops data-supported business cases, and coordinates execution across business lines and enabling functions. The role serves as a strategic connector across Distribution, Product, Technology, CRM, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Risk, and Compliance to align investments, capabilities, governance, and implementation priorities that support sustainable and profitable growth. Role Scope and Distinction ·    Own the translation of the Head of Distribution’s strategic direction into an integrated enterprise plan, business cases, sequenced priorities, and execution roadmaps. ·    Focus on enterprise strategy, market choices, cross-business alignment, and investment decisions rather than the day-to-day creation of seller-facing dashboards, targeting tools, and CRM insights led by Sales Enablement. ·    Partner with Risk and Compliance to understand regulatory and suitability boundaries; this role does not replace the independent oversight, interpretation, or approval responsibilities of those functions. Key Responsibilities Strategy Translation & Enterprise Planning ·    Convert the distribution strategy established by the Head of Distribution into a practical plan that defines where to play, how to compete, and which capabilities and investments are required. ·    Translate business objectives into strategic initiatives, implementation plans, governance structures, KPIs, and execution roadmaps. ·    Coordinate priorities across business lines and establish shared accountability for enterprise growth objectives. Market Intelligence & Business Case Development ·    Assess market, customer, advisor, competitor, and business-line data to identify additional markets and growth opportunities. ·    Understand how data from available tools and systems is integrated, evaluate the quality and relevance of the evidence, and use it to inform strategic choices. ·    Develop data-supported business cases that articulate opportunity size, strategic rationale, investment requirements, risks, dependencies, and expected business value. ·    Build a strong understanding of each business line to determine where enterprise distribution capabilities can connect, create value, and unlock growth. Cross-Functional Strategy & Integration ·    Partner with PO Growth & Development, Wealth Management, Product, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Operations, Technology, CRM, Marketing, and other business leaders to align strategy, investments, and execution priorities. ·    Connect business lines and enabling functions, ask the critical questions needed to resolve gaps, and ensure opportunities are evaluated from an enterprise perspective. ·    Drive technology and platform integration priorities that improve distribution effectiveness and advisor and customer experiences. CRM, Data & Sales Enablement Partnership ·    Define the strategic capabilities, data connections, and business requirements that Distribution needs from CRM and related platforms. ·    Partner with Sales Enablement to translate strategic priorities and integrated data into seller-facing actions, CRM enhancements, segmentation, dashboards, pipeline visibility, and cross-sell insights. ·    Partner with Marketing and other teams to strengthen connections among market insights, campaigns, advisor engagement, and sales execution. ·    Promote consistent data definitions, integration, quality, and governance across distribution and operational systems. Governance, Risk & Compliance Partnership ·    Identify regulatory, risk, compliance, and suitability considerations that may affect strategic options or implementation plans. ·    Engage Risk and Compliance early to define boundaries, assess third-party companies or capabilities related to suitability, and incorporate required controls into business cases and roadmaps. ·    Maintain clear decision rights so that Risk and Compliance functions retain responsibility for independent interpretation, oversight, and approvals. Executive Communication & Change Leadership ·    Create executive-level presentations, white papers, strategic recommendations, and board-ready materials that clearly frame choices and recommended actions. ·    Communicate the strategic narrative, decisions, tradeoffs, milestones, and expected outcomes to senior stakeholders. ·    Lead change across functions by building alignment, resolving dependencies, and maintaining momentum from strategy through implementation. Qualifications Required ·    10+ years of progressive experience in distribution strategy, sales strategy, enterprise strategy, or a related discipline within broker-dealer, RIA, insurance, wealth management, or financial services environments. ·    Demonstrated experience translating senior-leader strategy into enterprise plans, market choices, investment priorities, business cases, and implementation roadmaps. ·    Proven success working across sales, PO growth & development, wealth management, product, technology, CRM, marketing, operations, finance, risk, and compliance functions. ·    Experience using integrated market and business data to evaluate growth opportunities and support strategic recommendations. ·    Working knowledge of CRM platforms, data integration, analytics, and digital transformation initiatives. ·    Exceptional executive communication, PowerPoint development, strategic storytelling, and stakeholder-influence skills. Preferred ·    Experience evaluating new markets, distribution models, partnerships, or platform capabilities in a regulated environment. ·    Knowledge of suitability considerations and experience partnering with Risk and Compliance to establish strategic and operating boundaries. ·    Experience supporting executive committees or boards with decision-ready strategy materials. Job Description: Head of Distribution Sales Enablement Distribution Strategy  |  Sales Intelligence  |  CRM & AI Enablement Position Summary The Head of Distribution Sales Enablement transforms enterprise data, market and competitive intelligence, and customer insights into actionable sales strategies that accelerate distribution growth across Proprietary (PO) and Third-Party (3P) channels. The role leads the continued buildout and integration of CRM capabilities within Distribution, advances sales intelligence and performance measurement, and equips leaders and sales teams with clear guidance on which producers and opportunities to prioritize, why they matter, and how to engage them effectively. This leader also drives responsible adoption of AI-enabled tools within the sales ecosystem to improve targeting, productivity, and decision-making. Key Responsibilities Sales Enablement Strategy & Planning ·    Lead the Distribution sales enablement strategy, translating enterprise data, business priorities, and market insights into actionable growth plans for PO and 3P channels. ·    Establish sales planning disciplines, goal-setting methodologies, formulas, and performance measurement frameworks that support consistent execution and accountability. ·    Identify and prioritize growth, cross-sell, and relationship-expansion opportunities across business lines. CRM, Technology & AI Enablement ·    Lead the continued buildout, implementation, and integration of CRM capabilities within Distribution, ensuring alignment across sales, product, and business-line workflows. ·    Define business requirements and partner with technology and enterprise data teams to configure scalable CRM solutions, data connections, and user experiences. ·    Advance the use of AI-enabled capabilities within Salesforce and related sales tools, including selecting and applying appropriate digital assistants or bots to improve seller productivity and decision-making. ·    Drive adoption through practical enablement, governance, and change leadership so that tools are consistently embedded in sales routines. Sales Intelligence, Analytics & Reporting ·    Responsible for converting centralized data into actionable KPIs, dashboards, scorecards, and sales insights. ·    Oversee development of layered and interactive dashboards using Power BI and advanced Excel capabilities, including automation and macros where appropriate. ·    Provide internal intelligence on business performance, client and producer activity, pipeline, and opportunity trends, complemented by external market and competitive intelligence. ·    Translate complex findings into clear recommendations for sales managers, wholesalers, and distribution leaders. Producer Targeting & Opportunity Prioritization ·    Develop producer identification, segmentation, and targeting strategies for PO and 3P channels. ·    Determine which producers, firms, and market opportunities sales teams should pursue and articulate the rationale, value proposition, and recommended engagement approach. ·    Create tools and insights that support internal prioritization first, then enable more focused and effective external sales engagement. Enterprise Partnership & Data Stewardship ·    Partner closely with Enterprise Data, Technology, Product, and business-line teams to translate enterprise capabilities into practical Distribution solutions. ·    Provide Distribution business requirements and subject-matter expertise for data models while relying on enterprise data teams for core data architecture and engineering. ·    Promote data quality, consistent definitions, and responsible use of customer, producer, market, and competitive information. Leadership & Executive Communication ·    Build, develop, and lead a high-performing sales enablement and intelligence function. ·    Develop executive presentations, business reviews, white papers, and strategic recommendations that clearly connect insights to business decisions. ·    Champion a data-driven culture and influence leaders across Distribution to adopt consistent sales practices, tools, and performance measures. Qualifications Required ·    10+ years of progressive experience in sales enablement, distribution strategy, CRM, sales analytics, business intelligence, or a related discipline, including leadership responsibility. ·    Demonstrated experience building, implementing, or materially expanding CRM capabilities within a sales or distribution organization; Salesforce experience strongly preferred. ·    Experience leading teams responsible for sales analytics, performance management, reporting, or sales planning. ·    Advanced experience using Power BI and Excel to create dashboards, automate reporting, and translate data into decision-ready insights. ·    Working knowledge of AI-enabled sales capabilities, including practical use of AI features, digital assistants, or bots within CRM and sales workflows. ·    Proven ability to translate complex enterprise, customer, producer, market, and competitive information into focused sales strategies and actions. ·    Strong executive communication, presentation, stakeholder management, and change leadership skills. Preferred ·    Experience in financial services, insurance, wealth management, or a similarly regulated and distribution-intensive industry. ·    Experience in insurance business lines, specifically annuities, life insurance, executive benefits and disability insurance ·    Experience partnering with enterprise data and technology teams on data models, integrations, governance, and scalable analytics solutions. ·    Knowledge of both proprietary and third-party distribution models. Job Description: Is the opportunity to join a culture where “We Do the Right Thing,” and “We Courageously Shape Our Future Together” important to you? If so, Guardian is seeking a resolute motivated individual to join our team as a Senior Lead Financial Analyst. Recognized as the Client Solutions & Wealth Management (CSWM) subject-matter expert in financial and business analytics, the Financial Analyst, Wealth Management sets the analytical agenda that turns Park Avenue Wealth Management (PAWM) and Guardian Wealth Partners (GWP) into decisions. Operating with mastery-level expertise and little day-to-day oversight, this role owns the margin, profitability, and performance insight that shapes how the business allocates capital, prices and serves clients, and invests in growth. This role provides recommendations and supports business cases directly to inform decisions made by CSWM and enterprise leaders, and it contributes to the functional strategy for how Finance partners with the business. You will: • Drive financial planning & analysis for the PAWM business — lead planning, forecasting, and the management-reporting P&L; surface the key drivers and trends; and own the critical view of PAWM channel economics — margin at channel, client, and producer level — translating it into insight that drives capital allocation, pricing, and growth decisions. • Develop the business cases and ROI frameworks that govern enablement and investment decisions across distribution, channel, and expense (including Clearing & Execution) economics. • Lead complex, high-visibility analytical initiatives with notable risk and cross-functional dependencies — defining the execution strategy, not just the analysis — such as net-flow and margin insight, distribution economics, and cost-to-serve. • Build and own the financial models behind budgeting, forecasting, driver-based planning, and long-range planning for PAWM/GWP, setting the standard others build to. • Convey and communicate complex findings to senior leaders — translating analysis into clear recommendations that support decision-making across Finance and the business, including through effective presentations. • Act as advisor, mentor, and technical authority to colleagues at all levels, raising the analytical capability of the broader team. • Contribute to the functional finance strategy for PAWM/GWP — shaping how the team industrializes data, embeds AI/automation, and shifts from reporting toward strategic partnership. You are: • Resourceful and relentlessly curious, you transform a conceptual analytical framework into tangible insight by understanding the relationships between data and the business rules and processes that produce it. • Comfortable operating with minimal oversight in a complex environment, you independently locate, reconcile, and validate data, flagging and resolving issues before they become problems. • A confident communicator who develops a deep understanding of complex topics and translates results for stakeholders in clear, non-technical terms, iterating with leadership and subject-matter experts to rationalize and refine the value of your analysis — and to persuade when the answer is not the expected one. • A recognized expert others seek out — you anticipate where the business is heading and bring the analysis forward before the question is asked. You have: Required: • 7+ years' experience developing and presenting financial and business analytics, including to senior leadership. • 7+ years' experience analyzing financial statements and interpreting results, with mastery of the drivers behind them. • Advanced experience with Excel and other data/analytics tools, comfort building repeatable processes over large, complex, multi-source datasets, and fluency in applying automation and AI to industrialize analysis. Preferred: • Experience with Wealth Management economics in a financial services or insurance arena. • A track record of leading complex, cross-functional analytical initiatives with notable risk, and of influencing decisions beyond your own team. • Experience working across multiple business areas and/or lines of business (e.g., sales, finance, life, disability, wealth/brokerage, distribution), and demonstrated knowledge of the concepts, processes, and datasets inherent to those environments. • Experience partnering with multiple stakeholders in a fast driven environment. The role requires strong strategic thinking, architecture breadth, executive communication, and the ability to influence across a large, complex, and federated enterprise environment. Key Responsibilities: Enterprise Architecture Leadership Support the Head of Enterprise Architecture in developing and evolving enterprise architecture strategy , principles, standards, and target-state roadmaps. Define and maintain architecture perspectives across business, application, data, integration, cloud, platform, security, and AI-related capabilities as applicable. Own enterprise standards, target state, governance, exceptions, material technology decision frameworks Translate enterprise strategy and target-state direction into practical guidance for domain architecture and engineering teams. Promote alignment across business units, shared services, and technology domains. Strategic Architecture and Transformation Provide architecture leadership for major strategic initiatives, modernization programs, and enterprise-impacting technology decisions. Assess architecture options and recommend solutions that balance business value, cost, risk, resilience, time to market, and long-term maintainability. Support enterprise transformation through simplification, rationalization, modernization, and platform reuse. Identify opportunities to reduce duplication, retire legacy complexity, and improve interoperability across the enterprise. Governance and Decision Support Participate in and support enterprise architecture governance, standards councils, review boards, and strategic decision forums. Evaluate material technology decisions using approved enterprise frameworks, including buy, build, reuse, partner, and retire options. Review architecture proposals for compliance with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, and risk requirements. Support management of architecture exceptions, including rationale, risk analysis, remediation paths, and time-bound approvals. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with federated domain architects, platform leaders, engineering teams, data and AI teams, security, infrastructure, and business technology leaders to drive alignment. Facilitate resolution of cross-domain design issues, architecture conflicts, and overlapping capability decisions. Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across technology and business-aligned delivery organizations. Ensure architecture direction is understood and applied consistently across federated teams. Works with Business Unit heads and principal solution architects to translate enterprise direction into federated execution. Risk, Security, and Resilience Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, recoverability, and regulatory considerations into architecture guidance and recommendations. Partner with risk, security, and compliance stakeholders to ensure technology decisions align with enterprise control requirements. Assess the operational and architectural implications of technology choices in regulated and high-availability environments. Talent and Capability Development Mentor and coach architects and senior technology professionals. Contribute to architecture capability development, communities of practice, and architecture operating model maturity. Support common role expectations, competency models, and quality standards across the architecture function. Promote enterprise-first thinking, sound decision-making, and strong architecture discipline. Deep cross-domain expertise spanning applications, integration, data, AI, cloud, security, and platform strategy. Experience supporting or leading architecture for large-scale transformation initiatives in complex enterprise environments. Experience with architecture governance, standards development, target-state planning, and strategic technology decision-making. Proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority. Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Preferred Education and Experience Experience in insurance, financial services, healthcare, or another highly regulated industry. Experience in a federated technology organization with centralized architecture direction and distributed execution. Experience with cloud modernization, API strategies, platform engineering, data ecosystems, and enterprise integration. Familiarity with AI-enabled enterprise capabilities, automation, and emerging technology trends. Advanced degree and/or relevant certifications such as TOGAF, SAFe , AWS, Azure, GCP, or equivalent. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture principles, methods, and governance practices. Broad understanding of enterprise technology domains and cross-domain dependencies. Ability to develop target-state architecture and pragmatic transition approaches. Strong business acumen and ability to connect architecture decisions to business outcomes. Ability to assess tradeoffs among speed, cost, quality, risk, and strategic fit. Strong facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to communicate effectively with executive, business, and technical audiences. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity and lead through influence. Job Description: Is the opportunity to join a culture where “We Do the Right Thing,” and “We Courageously Shape Our Future Together” important to you? If so, Guardian is seeking a motivated individual to join our team as a Workforce Planning Consultant. This role will report to the Head of Workforce Management, Group Benefits and serve as a strategic workforce planning consultant, trusted advisor, and subject-matter expert. You will own and evolve workforce planning methodologies, lead complex scenario planning, and translate workforce data into executive-ready recommendations that influence staffing decisions. You will be a partner with business leaders, Finance, Human Resources, Operations, Technology, and other stakeholders to evaluate workforce risks, challenge assumptions, and develop practical workforce strategies aligned with financial, operational, customer, and colleague objectives. Working with significant autonomy, you will lead specialized initiatives, create customized solutions to complex workforce challenges, and strengthen workforce planning capability through mentorship and knowledge transfer. You will Own and evolve workforce planning methodologies, standards, assumptions, and governance to support consistent, transparent, and defensible workforce decisions. Lead complex workforce planning and scenario modeling efforts that evaluate demand, productivity, shrinkage, staffing, capacity, service, and operational risk. Develop executive-ready workforce recommendations that clearly communicate alternatives, trade-offs, risks, and a recommended course of action. Serve as a strategic advisor to senior business leaders by translating workforce insights into practical strategies aligned with business priorities and operating commitments. Challenge workforce assumptions and established approaches when business conditions, emerging risks, or opportunities require a different solution. Evaluate strategic staffing alternatives, including hiring, cross-training, vendor, channel, skill, productivity, and operating-model scenarios. Influence workforce investment and resource decisions through objective analysis, consultative partnership, and clear articulation of business impact. Identify emerging workforce risks and opportunities, recommend mitigation strategies, and provide decision support during periods of material business change or uncertainty. Partner with Finance and business stakeholders to connect workforce plans with budgets, forecasts, productivity commitments, headcount strategies, and long-range business plans. Lead complex or specialized workforce initiatives from problem definition through recommendation, stakeholder alignment, implementation support, and outcome review. Mentor workforce planning talent by providing technical guidance, sharing best practices, and strengthening consultative and analytical capabilities across the team. Communicate difficult concepts and recommendations to diverse audiences, adapting the message to build understanding, alignment, and action. You have Required Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in business, finance, mathematics, statistics, data science, analytics, or a related field, or comparable professional experience. 10+ years of experience in workforce management, workforce planning, capacity planning, workforce analytics, or a related discipline, with demonstrated ownership of complex planning work and business recommendations. Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to synthesize incomplete or conflicting information and develop customized solutions. Experience advising senior leaders, challenging assumptions constructively, explaining trade-offs, and influencing decisions without formal authority. Exceptional written, verbal, facilitation, and presentation skills, including the judgment and discretion required for sensitive workforce discussions. Proven ability to translate complex quantitative analysis into clear executive narratives, recommendations, and decisions. Experience leading complex or specialized projects across multiple stakeholders in a matrixed organization. A self-directed, collaborative, and improvement-oriented mindset, with the ability to manage competing priorities and operate effectively with guidance only in the most complex situations. Preferred Qualifications: Specialized expertise in workforce forecasting, staffing and capacity modeling, scenario planning, productivity analysis, shrinkage, service-level dynamics, and workforce risk assessment in both back office and contact center environments. Demonstrated ability to design, adapt, and govern workforce planning methodologies rather than only apply established models. Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect workforce decisions to service, cost, quality, customer, colleague, and operational outcomes. Expert proficiency with analytical and presentation tools such as Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with workforce management, data visualization, forecasting, or modeling platforms such as Verint, Tableau, or comparable tools. Experience mentoring analysts or serving as a technical advisor and thought leader within a workforce planning or analytics function. Job Description: Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability Reports To Head of Technology Operations Department Enterprise Technology Position Summary The Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability is responsible for defining and executing the enterprise observability strategy, operating model, and platform roadmap that enable proactive, predictive, and resilient technology operations. This leader owns the enterprise capabilities for monitoring, telemetry, event intelligence, operational analytics, and observability engineering, ensuring technology services are observable, measurable, actionable, and continuously improving. The role serves as the operational intelligence leader across Enterprise Technology, providing the platforms, standards, insights, and governance required to improve service reliability, accelerate issue detection and resolution, and support modern operational practices. This leader partners closely with infrastructure, cloud, middleware, application, security, resiliency, and service management teams to build a unified enterprise-wide observability capability. Key Responsibilities Enterprise Observability Strategy Define and execute the enterprise observability vision, strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap. Establish standards and governance for monitoring, logging, metrics, tracing, telemetry, alerting, and service observability. Lead the evolution of observability capabilities from reactive monitoring toward proactive, predictive, and automated operations. Drive enterprise adoption of modern observability practices, frameworks, and engineering standards. Observability Platform Ownership Own the strategy, architecture, lifecycle, and operation of enterprise monitoring and observability platforms. Lead platform modernization, tool rationalization, capability expansion, and service offering improvements. Manage vendor relationships, contracts, platform investments, and cost optimization efforts. Ensure scalability, availability, resilience, and ongoing enhancement of observability tooling and services. Monitoring and Telemetry Services Establish enterprise monitoring and instrumentation standards across infrastructure, cloud, middleware, applications, databases, and digital services. Improve monitoring coverage, telemetry quality, alert effectiveness, signal quality, and operational visibility. Drive adoption of distributed tracing, service dependency mapping, and end-to-end transaction monitoring. Ensure service health and operational data are consistently available across the technology landscape. Operational Intelligence and AIOps Lead implementation of operational analytics, event intelligence, anomaly detection, predictive insights, and AIOps capabilities. Develop dashboards, scorecards, and reporting that provide actionable operational intelligence to technology leadership. Enable intelligent event correlation, noise reduction, automated diagnostics, and automated operational workflows. Partner with engineering and operations teams to use observability data for continuous improvement and outage prevention. Reliability and Incident Enablement Partner with technology teams to improve detection, response, recovery, and root cause analysis capabilities. Establish observability practices that improve service reliability, operational resilience, and customer experience. Drive post-incident learning and identification of automation opportunities. Provide enterprise visibility into technology health, performance trends, capacity risks, and reliability risks. Leadership and Talent Development Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of observability engineers, platform engineers, and operational intelligence specialists. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, operational excellence, continuous learning, and cross-functional partnership. Lead organizational adoption of observability best practices through enablement, coaching, and stakeholder engagement. Establish strong partnerships across technology, cybersecurity, architecture, engineering, operations, resiliency, and service management functions. Qualifications 10+ years of experience in infrastructure operations, platform engineering, observability, reliability engineering, or related technology disciplines. 5+ years of experience leading enterprise-scale engineering or operational teams. Deep expertise in observability platforms, monitoring technologies, telemetry pipelines, logging, metrics, distributed tracing, and operational analytics. Demonstrated experience implementing enterprise monitoring strategies and improving operational reliability at scale. Strong understanding of cloud platforms, hybrid infrastructure, automation, DevOps practices, and modern operational architectures. Experience leading organizational transformation and driving adoption of new operational capabilities. Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and strategic planning skills. Success Measures Increased enterprise monitoring and observability coverage. Reduced mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR). Improved signal quality and reduced alert fatigue. Increased adoption of observability standards and platform capabilities. Improved service reliability, operational resilience, and operational efficiency. Expansion of predictive analytics, automation, and AIOps capabilities across Enterprise Technology. Job Title: Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation
Job Description: The Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation is a senior leadership role responsible for the strategic evolution, differentiation, and commercial success of our open‑architecture wealth management product platform. This individual wakes up every day thinking about what’s next —how product, partners, packaging, and go‑to‑market strategy come together to create a compelling, modern, and advisor‑centric platform across fee‑based advisory, annuities, and alternatives. We do not manufacture products. Our competitive advantage comes from curation, partnership, design, positioning, and delivery . This role exists to ensure our platform is not merely comprehensive—but distinctive, relevant, and growth‑oriented . The role works horizontally across the organization —marketing, sales, business development, training, product management—and externally with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and portfolio managers . Success requires influence without direct ownership, entrepreneurial energy, and a strong commercial mindset. Key Responsibilities Product Strategy & Innovation Own the forward‑looking product strategy across advisory, annuities, and alternatives within an open‑architecture ecosystem. Identify gaps, white spaces, and emerging opportunities driven by advisor needs, client behavior, regulation, and competitive dynamics. Design differentiated product constructs, solutions, and portfolios by creatively leveraging third‑party partners rather than manufacturing products. Translate industry trends (e.g., retirement income, tax efficiency, private markets, managed solutions, model portfolios) into actionable platform initiatives. Platform Differentiation & Go‑to‑Market Develop clear go‑to‑market strategies for platform capabilities, including positioning, messaging, and advisor value propositions. Partner closely with Marketing to ensure product stories are simple, compelling, and commercially effective . Work with Sales and Business Development to align product strategy with advisor adoption, growth objectives, and field readiness . Drive clarity around why advisors should use specific solutions—not just what is available. Partner Strategy & Ecosystem Management Serve as a senior point of engagement with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and product sponsors . Evaluate, onboard, and rationalize partners with a focus on quality, differentiation, economics, and strategic fit . Co‑create solutions with partners where appropriate, including custom portfolios, white‑labeled offerings, or exclusive access strategies . Maintain a strong commercial lens on platform economics, scalability, and advisor impact. Cross‑Functional Leadership & Influence Act as a strategic connector across Product Management, Sales, Marketing, Training, and Business Development. Provide strategic direction while leveraging existing execution teams for implementation. Influence priorities and outcomes without direct people ownership , using clarity, credibility, and collaboration. Partner with Training and Sales Enablement to ensure advisors understand not just products—but how to use them in holistic planning conversations . Job Description: Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Understand and participate across portfolio initiatives, connect dependencies and opportunities across programs to optimize solutions, increase reuse, and reduce data waste. Drive the adoption of a data product operating model across the organization. Champion data product thinking by promoting customer-centric design, product ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable business value. Establish best practices for discoverability, usability, interoperability, governance, and consumption of enterprise data products. Translate business strategy into scalable technology, data, and analytics solutions. Lead discovery workshops and data solution design sessions across underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, reporting, and digital channels. Influence enterprise technology strategy by identifying reusable capabilities and modernization opportunities. Develop reusable frameworks, accelerators, and reference architectures to improve data delivery speed, consistency, and reuse. Design modern data platforms and pipelines that support real-time and batch processing, scalable data integration, and enterprise analytics needs. Ensure high-quality, trusted data through governance, observability, lineage, metadata, and automated data quality controls. Collaborate with data engineering, product, and AI teams to operationalize AI-enabled data solutions within the data ecosystem. Foster collaboration across architecture, engineering, product management, security, data, AI, and business teams. Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems, including application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows. Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority.
